[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Identifying and Mitigating Slow Queries in PostgreSQL"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Database performance degradation often stems from inefficient queries. In PostgreSQL, identifying these bottlenecks requires leveraging built-in statistics tools and query analyzers to pinpoint issues and apply appropriate mitigations."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Enabling and Configuring pg_stat_statements"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The pg_stat_statements module tracks execution statistics of all SQL statements executed by a server. To enable it, modify your postgresql.conf file and restart the database service."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"shared_preload_libraries = 'pg_stat_statements'
pg_stat_statements.track = all"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once enabled, create the extension in your target database by running the following command."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_stat_statements;"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Finding the Slowest Queries"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can query the pg_stat_statements view to identify statements consuming the most total execution time. This helps prioritize which queries to optimize first."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"SELECT 
    total_exec_time AS total_time,
    calls,
    mean_exec_time AS mean_time,
    query
FROM pg_stat_statements
ORDER BY total_exec_time DESC
LIMIT 10;"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Analyzing Execution Plans with EXPLAIN ANALYZE"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"After identifying a problematic query, use the EXPLAIN ANALYZE command to understand how the PostgreSQL query planner executes it. Be cautious running this on write-heavy queries in production."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = 'example@test.com';"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Look for Sequential Scans (Seq Scan) on large tables, which indicate missing indexes."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Check for high startup costs and discrepancies between estimated and actual row counts."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Mitigating Performance Issues"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Common mitigation strategies in PostgreSQL include:"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Adding appropriate B-tree or Hash indexes for columns frequently used in WHERE clauses and JOIN conditions."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Running ANALYZE regularly to ensure the query planner has up-to-date statistics about table distributions."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Refactoring complex queries, breaking down subqueries, or using Common Table Expressions (CTEs) wisely."}]
